card: PR #36109 extracts block template reconstruction for arbitrary parent blocks into a shared SwitchBlockParent test utility used by BuildChain and MinerTestingSetup::Block. It recalculates the proof-of-work target and block subsidy directly from the target parent, pads coinbase scriptSigs with an OP_0 dummy push to satisfy BIP 34 minimum length rules on heights 1 through 16, and enforces coinbase-only templates to prevent discarding transaction fees. This resolves bad-cb-amount and bad-cb-length validation errors encountered when test fixtures generate reorgs near genesis or across halving boundaries.
changed_since_previous: No substantive changes to the approach or implementation since the previous review; minor rebase or comment cleanups.
evidence: PR description: 'Test helpers that attach active-tip templates to arbitrary parents retain the template's subsidy. Existing reorg tests can pass with underpaid coinbases. A fork crossing a halving can overpay and fail with bad-cb-amount. At heights 1 through 16, encoding only the height leaves the coinbase input script too short and triggers bad-cb-length.'
Commit bf551335be characterization test demonstrates that unpadded low-height coinbases and halving rewards previously prevented connecting forks built from genesis.
problem: Test utilities creating block forks from arbitrary ancestor blocks re-used active-tip block templates without adjusting subsidy or difficulty for the target parent. As a result, forks crossing halving boundaries could overpay and fail validation with bad-cb-amount, while forks starting at heights 1 through 16 lacked coinbase script padding and failed with bad-cb-length.

risk.why: Mistakes only affect test block construction helpers, causing unit tests to fail to build or connect test chains.

summary: Consolidates parent-dependent block template reconstruction into a shared SwitchBlockParent test utility used by BuildChain and MinerTestingSetup::Block. The helper updates the previous block hash, timestamp, and merkle root while recalculating difficulty (nBits) and the coinbase subsidy from the actual parent rather than the active chain tip. It also appends an OP_0 dummy push to coinbase scriptSigs so heights 1 through 16 meet minimum script length requirements, and asserts templates contain only a coinbase transaction.
